name: Battle of Waterloo

sides.name: Seventh Coalition (Anglo-Allied and Prussian)
sides.commander: Arthur Wellesley, Duke of Wellington (Anglo-Allied), Gebhard von Blücher (Prussian)
sides.strength: About 68,000 Anglo-Allied troops on the ridge of Mont-Saint-Jean, with around 50,000 Prussians arriving from Wavre through the afternoon
sides.casualties: Around 23,000 killed and wounded across both Coalition armies

sides.name: First French Empire
sides.commander: Napoleon Bonaparte (Emperor), Michel Ney (left wing), Emmanuel de Grouchy (detached pursuing the Prussians)
sides.strength: About 73,000 troops of the Armée du Nord including the Imperial Guard
sides.casualties: Around 25,000 killed and wounded, 7,000 captured; the army shattered

summary: Napoleon attacked Wellington's line on the ridge of Mont-Saint-Jean from 11:30 onward, hoping to defeat the Anglo-Allied army before the Prussians could intervene. The French squandered the afternoon in costly attacks: D'Erlon's infantry assault on the centre was broken by the Union and Household Brigades; Ney's massed cavalry charges crashed against the Allied infantry squares; the farm complex of Hougoumont held against repeated French infantry attacks all day. The Prussian IV Corps reached Plancenoit by 16:30 and tied down Lobau's reserve. The Imperial Guard's last attack about 19:30 broke against fresh British battalions, and the whole French line collapsed.
significance: Waterloo ended Napoleon's Hundred Days and the Napoleonic Wars, sending the emperor into final exile on Saint Helena where he died six years later. The Congress of Vienna's settlement that followed governed European international politics for the next century. The battle became a permanent reference point for political and cultural events whose consequences are felt long after the day they were decided.
